correctness.rationale: Independent azimuth integration gives the whole law. Fold azimuth by prism symmetry into φ in [0,π/6]; the vertical component of an upper-hemisphere uniform normal is uniform on [0,1]. Set g(c)=c/sqrt(c²+t²). Conditionally, the triangular case has probability 1−g(cos φ). A pentagon occurs precisely when the unscaled threshold lies between cos(π/3+φ) and cos(π/3−φ), so its conditional probability is g(cos(π/3−φ))−g(cos(π/3+φ)). Integrating using sin φ as the variable gives the stated p3 and p5, with p4 the remainder; the generic sign patterns give no other types. The stationary factor decreases strictly from 1 to 3/2−sqrt(3), proving the unique maximum. A bounded independent bisection reproduced t=0.53146955106361, 2t/sqrt(3)=0.61368817674533 and p5=0.38515580567418. Replay: python3 /workspace/review-evidence/5/check_prism.py. The analytic proof, not any grid or Monte Carlo check, covers all t>0. Frozen checker and verification notes were inspected, not executed.
